texts: bad: the per-lantern rule hands every lantern one and the same portion of mire-essence (it reuses a single essence symbol as each lantern's object), which the sentence does not say, and "extra" on a mass noun has no licensed quantity carrier, so it lands on an invented marker. Rewrite so each lantern gets its own countable portion and "extra" can ride as an ordinary adjective: "Each lantern of the three Cliff Path stations burns an extra ration of mire-essence."

mixed: the query correctly reuses the lanterns' group symbol, but with the verb left open the undergoer's role has to be guessed, and it guesses Patient while the premise stores these lanterns as the burning event's agent, so nothing binds. Either name the consequence — "Do the lanterns of those stations burn out?" — or, to keep the verb open, use the one licensed open template, "What do the lanterns of those stations do?", which binds the stored burning event.
